newsitem.title: USA: California car-wash said to launder drug money.
newsitem.headline: California car-wash said to launder drug money.

text.p: A federal grand jury has returned a 23-count indictment charging 13 people in a drug-smuggling ring run out of a southern California car-wash company, prosecutors said on Thursday.

The charges came after a six-year investigation into the business dealings of Fernando Ramirez Cortez, who allegedly controlled a cocaine distribution network that stretched from Mexico to Chicago, U.S. Attorney Nora Manella said.
Ramirez, 40, known as "My Friend", was arrested on June 24 along with his wife Evelyn, Manella said in a statement.
Ramirez allegedly used his Universal Car Equipment Inc. car-wash company in Ontario, California, as a cover to launder drug proceeds.

Prosecutors said federal law enforcement agents monitored Ramirez' telephone conversations, revealing he and associates negotiated shipments of cocaine from various suppliers, including an organisation in Mexicali, Mexico.
Large quantities of the drug were delivered to the Chicago area, including one 440-pound (200 kg) shipment in last October.

The wiretaps also revealed that $2 million in cash was transported in vehicles with secret compartments. Two people working for Ramirez allegedly transported hundreds of thousands of dollars in cash from Chicago to Los Angeles hidden in car spare tires.
Two other people allegedly strapped tens of thousands of dollars to their bodies to bring cash to California, Manella's statement said.

Besides Ramirez and his wife, seven people, including suspected Mexicali drug lord Segundo Valenzuela, were arrested June 23 in Los Angeles. Four more suspects were detained in Chicago. They face a variety of narcotics and money-laundering charges.
In addition, agents seized five homes, one commercial property, three motor homes and more than a dozen passenger and recreational vehicles.
